newsitem.title: USA: Virgin's Branson blasts British Air "arrogance".
newsitem.headline: Virgin's Branson blasts British Air "arrogance".

text.p: Virgin Group President Richard Branson Wednesday accused British Airways Plc Chief Executive Robert Ayling of "breathtaking arrogance" in linking approval of his company's proposed alliance with AMR Corp's American Airlines to support a U.S.-Britain open skies agreement.
"Who made Robert Ayling and (AMR Chairman) Bob Crandall the arbiters of British and U.S. national aviation policy," Branson asked at a news conference.
"With breathtaking arrogance, Mr. Ayling has said if they're not granted antitrust immunity, there will be no open skies agreement between the United States and Great Britain," he said.
Branson said American Airlines had made similar statements on its Website.

British Airways threatened Wednesday to abandon the proposed alliance with American and, with it, support for an open skies aviation trade deal if regulatory approvals were not granted before November.
"Since when do decisions affecting the wellbeing of the people of the U.S. and the U.K. get made by two private companies?" Branson said.
Branson also predicted the proposed BA-American alliance would not go through, saying he "would bet money on it not happening."
"The longer it goes on, the more optimistic we're getting," he said.

Branson spoke ahead of a scheduled appearance before the House aviation subcommittee at which Crandall, Ayling and other airline executives were also to testify. But the hearing was postponed due to the press of full House business.
